note.en: Thumb inside the cuff pointing down, fingers outside, like a pistol.
A pistol grip is allowed with a positive attitude and time is given to prepare an attack. Held passively, or used to block, it draws a shido.

about.en: The sleeve is taken at the cuff with the thumb pointing down inside it and the fingers wrapped round the outside. It locks the wrist and lets the whole arm be lifted and turned, which is what the one-arm shoulder throw and the sleeve-lifting hip throw want; held without attacking it is a penalty.

en: Thumb down into the cuff, fingers round the outside
The grip lifts and turns the arm; it does not pull
Attack straight away, or let it go
Take your partner's cuff with your thumb pointing down inside the sleeve end and your fingers closed round the outside.
Lift and turn the arm with that hand while the other takes the lapel.
Turn in under the lifted arm at once.

receiving.en: A thumb inside your cuff means your arm is about to be lifted and you are about to be turned under it. Bend the elbow hard and pull the hand to your hip; the pistol grip is weak against a bent arm.

viNotes.en: The thumb inside your sleeve end is a very particular feeling and worth learning to recognise: the attack under that arm follows immediately.
